exact_statement: For a nonnegative absolutely continuous active-enzyme abundance satisfying dE/dt=p-gamma*E, E(0)=E0, with measurable envelopes 0<=p<=pbar, gamma>=gamma_lower>=0 and catalytic turnover kcat<=kbar, the abundance is bounded by Ebar(t)=E0 exp(-Gamma(t))+integral_0^t pbar(s) exp(-(Gamma(t)-Gamma(s))) ds, Gamma(t)=integral_0^t gamma_lower. A forward flux v_j<=chi*kbar*E therefore satisfies integral_0^T v_j<=integral_0^T chi*kbar*Ebar. Thermodynamic gate chi is zero only when the measured Gibbs interval robustly forbids forward flux; uncertain direction retains chi=1.
assumptions: specific synthesis p and dilution/degradation gamma share consistent biomass basis
TFA directionality used only with a declared strict Gibbs margin
status: internally derived elementary comparison lemma; sharp in the stated reduced interface; scientific novelty not claimed
novelty_boundary: Dynamic enzyme-cost FBA and dynamic regulatory enzyme-cost FBA already model transient enzyme, substrate, and flux trajectories. This is a necessary post-hoc certificate, not a new framework or network-level objective theorem.
costs: measure active enzyme abundance and uncertainty
measure or bound enzyme synthesis per biomass
measure metabolite activities, transformed standard Gibbs energy, temperature, pH, ionic strength
charge time-resolved isotope flux measurements and proteomics
falsifier: On a pre-registered interval, a lower confidence bound for observed forward flux integral exceeds the computed conservative upper bound; or positive forward flux occurs when the lower Gibbs bound is strictly positive under the chosen TFA convention.
next_gate: Apply to a pre-registered enzyme-induction time course and compare against matched deFBA/r-deFBA and a kinetic ODE model; only pursue as research novelty if it yields a network-level bound or held-out prediction gain.

exact_statement: For one downhill enzyme-limited reaction with capacity v<=kE, fixed proteome cap E<=Emax, initial E0=0, synthesis p<=gamma*Emax, constant gamma>0, and nonlimiting upstream/downstream fluxes, static eFBA/TFA has optimum kEmax while the sharp dynamic instantaneous flux is kEmax(1-exp(-gamma*t)); the horizon-average maximum is kEmax[1-(1-exp(-gamma*T))/(gamma*T)].
assumptions: fixed reaction direction with measured DeltaG<=-g<0
same fixed saturation factor is included in k for static and dynamic comparators
reaction is the static objective and other network constraints have slack
only enzyme abundance dynamics distinguish the models
status: exact reduced-model counterexample derived; broad conceptual point is established prior art
novelty_boundary: Does not establish that every cell follows the reduced one-enzyme model; deFBA/r-deFBA already model the broad transient-vs-steady distinction.
costs: turnover, active enzyme, synthesis, dilution/degradation, substrate saturation, Gibbs-energy measurements
falsifier: In an isolated matched system, validated parameter intervals yield measured average flux above the exact dynamic ceiling.
next_gate: Use inducible single-copy lacZ with constitutive lacY and matched low/high pre-expression reserves, then compare against dynamic controls.
